entries.name: com.apple.AppleSunriseBluetooth
entries.note: Driver for the Bluetooth controller on Apple hardware; BifrOSt targets generic PC and tablet hardware with the Linux kernel's own Bluetooth drivers.

entries.name: com.apple.AppleSunriseWLAN
entries.note: Driver for the Wi-Fi chip on Apple hardware; BifrOSt uses the Linux wireless drivers on other hardware.

entries.name: com.apple.AppleUserHIDDrivers
entries.note: Covers the HID device model the apps read; the kernel's evdev and HID drivers read the hardware, and this row does not replace them. Verified on the midget with BifrOSt 0.10.16 (os_verify).
entries.ready_note: The HID device model is tested in hid_devices.rs. The kernel usbhid and hid_generic drivers read the hardware (usbhid is built in on the reference kernel).

entries.name: com.apple.DriverKit-Apple16X50PCI
entries.note: Not determined as a BifrOSt component: a 16550 UART PCI serial driver whose counterpart is the Linux kernel serial driver; no kernel package is cited because runtime-packages.txt does not list one. Verified on the midget with BifrOSt 0.10.16 (os_verify).
entries.ready_note: 16550 UART ports are driven by the Linux 8250 serial driver (built in on the Arch kernel), which BifrOSt ships unchanged.

entries.name: com.apple.DriverKit-AppleBCMWLAN
entries.note: The chip is driven by the Linux kernel (brcmfmac for Broadcom parts). BifrOSt covers the layer above it: scans, joins and saved profiles through wpa_supplicant, and power save through nl80211. It does not configure the chip or its firmware. Verified on the midget with BifrOSt 0.10.16 (os_verify).
entries.ready_note: brcmfmac drives the Broadcom chip. The layer above it (scans, joins, saved profiles through wpa_supplicant, nl80211 power save) is covered by the wifi, wpa and nl80211 tests.

entries.name: com.apple.DriverKit-AppleEthernetE1000
entries.note: The Intel gigabit cards are driven by the Linux e1000 and e1000e kernel modules. netd takes the address by DHCP. BifrOSt has no per-card settings such as offload or wake-on-LAN. Verified on the midget with BifrOSt 0.10.16 (os_verify).
entries.ready_note: The e1000 and e1000e kernel modules drive the cards; netd takes the address by DHCP and has tests.

entries.name: com.apple.DriverKit-AppleEthernetIXGBE
entries.note: The Intel 10 GbE cards are driven by the Linux ixgbe kernel module. netd manages them like any other link. BifrOSt has no tuning surface for queues or offloads. Verified on the midget with BifrOSt 0.10.16 (os_verify).
entries.ready_note: The ixgbe kernel module drives the 10 GbE cards; netd manages the link.

entries.name: com.apple.DriverKit-AppleEthernetIXL
entries.note: The Intel 700-series cards (XL710 family) are driven by the Linux i40e kernel module. netd manages them like any other link. BifrOSt has no tuning surface for these cards. Verified on the midget with BifrOSt 0.10.16 (os_verify).
entries.ready_note: The i40e kernel module drives the 700-series cards; netd manages the link.

entries.name: com.apple.DriverKit-AppleEthernetMLX5
entries.note: The ConnectX cards are driven by the Linux mlx5_core kernel module, and rdma-core is the userspace verbs layer. netd manages the links like any other. BifrOSt has no RDMA or offload surface for apps. Verified on the midget with BifrOSt 0.10.16 (os_verify).
entries.ready_note: The mlx5_core kernel module drives the ConnectX cards and rdma-core is the userspace verbs layer (runtime-packages.txt); netd manages the links.

entries.name: com.apple.DriverKit-AppleUSBCHCOM
entries.note: WCH CH34x USB serial adapters are handled by the Linux ch341 kernel module, which creates a /dev/ttyUSB node. BifrOSt exposes no serial-port API to apps, so the device stays with the OS. Verified on the midget with BifrOSt 0.10.16 (os_verify).
entries.ready_note: The ch341 kernel module drives CH34x adapters and creates /dev/ttyUSB nodes.

entries.name: com.apple.DriverKit-AppleUSBFTDI
entries.note: FTDI USB serial adapters are handled by the Linux ftdi_sio kernel module, which creates a /dev/ttyUSB node. BifrOSt exposes no serial-port API to apps, so the device stays with the OS. Verified on the midget with BifrOSt 0.10.16 (os_verify).
entries.ready_note: The ftdi_sio kernel module drives FTDI adapters and creates /dev/ttyUSB nodes.

entries.name: com.apple.DriverKit-AppleUSBPLCOM
entries.note: Prolific PL2303 USB serial adapters are handled by the Linux pl2303 kernel module, which creates a /dev/ttyUSB node. BifrOSt exposes no serial-port API to apps, so the device stays with the OS. Verified on the midget with BifrOSt 0.10.16 (os_verify).
entries.ready_note: The pl2303 kernel module drives PL2303 adapters and creates /dev/ttyUSB nodes.

entries.name: com.apple.DriverKit-AppleUSBSLCOM
entries.note: Silicon Labs CP210x USB serial adapters are handled by the Linux cp210x kernel module, which creates a /dev/ttyUSB node. BifrOSt exposes no serial-port API to apps, so the device stays with the OS. Verified on the midget with BifrOSt 0.10.16 (os_verify).
entries.ready_note: The cp210x kernel module drives CP210x adapters and creates /dev/ttyUSB nodes.

entries.name: com.apple.DriverKit-AppleUSBSerial
entries.note: The generic USB serial class is part of the Linux USB serial core, which gives adapters without a vendor driver a /dev/ttyUSB node. BifrOSt exposes no serial-port API to apps, so the device stays with the OS. Verified on the midget with BifrOSt 0.10.16 (os_verify).
entries.ready_note: The Linux USB serial core (usbserial, built in on the reference kernel) gives vendor-less adapters a /dev/ttyUSB node.

entries.name: com.apple.DriverKit-IOUserDockChannelSerial
entries.note: A serial channel inside the reference vendor's silicon laptops that links the machine to its built-in dock controller. PC hardware has no such channel, so the component has no meaning on this system.

entries.name: com.apple.DriverKit-UVCUserService
entries.note: USB video class cameras are driven by the Linux uvcvideo kernel module. BifrOSt captures frames through V4L2 (v4l2.rs) and runs the camera app on top of them. No SDK API lets apps open a camera. Verified on the midget with BifrOSt 0.10.16 (os_verify).
entries.ready_note: uvcvideo drives USB video class cameras; v4l2.rs and the camera app's tests cover the capture layer above it.

entries.name: com.apple.DriverKit.AppleUserECM
entries.note: USB Ethernet adapters that use the CDC Ethernet Control Model are driven by the Linux cdc_ether kernel module. netd manages them like any other link. BifrOSt has no adapter-specific settings. Verified on the midget with BifrOSt 0.10.16 (os_verify).
entries.ready_note: The cdc_ether kernel module drives CDC Ethernet adapters; netd manages the link.
